messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: ForgeBridge SDK conformance & runtime tracing runbook

Hi Emily / Benedict —

Thanks again for the intro call last week. As discussed, we want to put together a practical conformance runbook so ForgeBridge can ship its LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs with first-class instrumentation for Redwood’s runtime (traces, token attribution, and KV cache compatibility).

I've attached an initial compatibility matrix (fb-compatibility-matrix.xlsx) that maps the SDK surface to Redwood trace hooks and model variant expectations. Quick ask: could you confirm which LangChain adapter patterns you currently support (LLMChain vs. agent vs. tool-only) so we can prioritize tests?

Proposed next steps:
- ForgeBridge: confirm adapter patterns + share SDK repo link and test credentials (sandbox).
- Redwood: produce a v1 runbook (trace-runbook-v1.md) and a short acceptance checklist for sandbox tests.
- Align on SOW items and billing for dedicated sandbox time — tagging Legal early so we can move fast.

Tentative timeline: conformance matrix + runbook draft by 04/12, sandbox tests week of 04/19, sign SOW by end of April.

Attaching: fb-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (summary sheet + test cases).

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ForgeBridge SDK conformance & runtime tracing runbook

Jonas — thanks, this is great. We support LLMChain, agent workflows, and a lightweight tool-only interface. Two quick notes:

1) Tracing: we ship a hooks abstraction (FBTrace) but currently serialize traces as JSON blobs inside our telemetry pipeline. We’re open to adding structured span IDs if Redwood requires it — can you sketch the minimal shape you need?

2) LlamaIndex: we have a custom serializer for embeddings that flattens metadata; curious whether Redwood’s KV cache requires exact bytes for cache hits, or if content-hash matching is sufficient.

Attaching our SDK spec and current trace abstraction (sdk-specs.pdf).

On the timeline: 04/12 for a draft runbook works. We’ll also share a sandbox service account by 04/10.

Best,
Emily
Director, Product — ForgeBridge

Subject: Re: ForgeBridge SDK conformance & runtime tracing runbook (internal notes)

Internal notes for the runbook draft — tagging here so we have an audit trail and can cut the doc quickly: 

- Minimal trace payload we need: span_id, parent_span_id (optional), event_type (request|response|cache_hit|cache_miss), token_count, model_variant, prompt_hash. JSON shape of ~6 fields is OK.
- For token attribution we require token-level offsets for generated text when the application requests attribution; acceptable fallback is prompt-level attribution.
- KV cache: content-hash matching is preferred (sha256 over canonicalized prompt+metadata). Exact-bytes can be brittle across serializers.
- Rollout phases: Sandbox conformance -> Canary (10% traffic with cache bypass) -> Full traffic (with automatic rollback on error budget).

I’ll draft trace-runbook-v1.md with these as acceptance criteria and lightweight curl + python examples to instrument the SDK.

Karthik
Senior Product — Runtime & Observability

Subject: Re: ForgeBridge SDK conformance & runtime tracing runbook — next steps and schedule

Emily / Benedict — thanks for the quick turn. Agreement on the high-level approach — next steps consolidated below and owners assigned.

1) Runbook / test cases (owner: Karthik) — Karthik to circulate trace-runbook-v1.md by EOD 04/23. Acceptance criteria include: trace spans with span_id + event_type, cache hit rates measured against content-hash, and token-attribution toggles validated in sandbox.
2) Sandbox access (owner: Emily) — ForgeBridge to send service account + test keys by 04/10 (noting Emily already committed to this).
3) Commercials & SOW (owner: Marissa) — Redwood legal to review redwood-fb-sow-v1.pdf; propose 04/27 for final signature.
4) Canary plan (owner: Vanessa) — canary to run at 10% for 72 hours with automatic rollback if error rate > 1% or latency SLO breach > 10% relative to baseline.

Meeting: I’ve scheduled a 30-min checkpoint on 04/26 to review initial sandbox results and confirm go/no-go for the canary. Link: https://meet.redwood.com/j/forgebridge-integration (also added to the shared drive).

If there are any blockers from Legal or Product Security on residency/retention windows, flag immediately so we can surface to execs.

Thanks — looking forward to shipping this.

Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
